input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 allocates deliverable ownership the wrong way for us. The default is Type II Materials, which IBM or third parties own outright, so any deliverable IBM fails to designate becomes IBM property even though we paid for it; our licence back is limited to use/reproduce/display/distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" with no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense. Conversely, for Type I Materials that we do own, we grant IBM an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence to distribute externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit and pass on our work product. There is also no statement anywhere (Sections 11.6, 14.17, 14.18) that we retain ownership of Content, Customer Components or our data; 14.17 grants only express licences, so silence is unhelpful. Redline flips the default to Type I (Customer-owned), confines IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials to internal use needed to perform the Services, upgrades the Type II licence to a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense for our business, and adds an express Customer Data/Content ownership and no-joint-ownership sentence.

proposal.summary: Flip Materials default to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence-back, narrow IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials, and confirm Customer ownership of Content/Customer Components.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so we have flipped the Section 7 default to Type I (Customer-owned) Materials, limited IBM's licence in those Customer-owned Materials to internal use needed to perform the Services, and expanded the Type II licence-back to a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense embedded IBM IP for our business. We have also confirmed that no Content, Customer Components or Customer data is assigned to IBM; if IBM prefers, we can accept the fallback of IBM retaining its generic tools and know-how so long as this licence-back and data ownership language stands.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.
ops.newText: distribute internally copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials, in each case solely as necessary to perform the Services; and 2. the right to authorize its Subcontractors to do any of the same solely for that purpose.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, distribute and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes.

ops.text: e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components, or any other Customer data, and IBM's rights therein are limited to the licenses expressly granted for the purpose of performing the Services. No Materials or other work product will be jointly owned.
